newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FUND SEES SKK 750MLN IN 1997 EXPORT SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FUND SEES SKK 750MLN IN 1997 EXPORT SUPPORT.

text.p: A Slovak state fund, set up to help curb the country's burgeoning foreign trade deficit, said on Tuesday its funds available for export support would total about 750 million crowns this year.

The State Fund to Support Exports (SFPE) aims to help primarily small and medium-sized companies launch or expand export activities, said chairman Slavomir Hatina, who is also a director of one of the largest exporters, oil refiner Slovnaft.
"The fund is an example of solidarity of large exporters, such as our company, with small firms that may have difficulties in entering foreign markets," he told a news conference.
Any Slovak company involved in foreign trade must contribute to the fund with 0.1 percent of its annual export-import turnover.
Hatina said that according to overall Slovak foreign trade turnover in 1996, the contribution of companies should total some 500 million crowns this year.
The 1997 state budget will allocate a further 250 million to the fund.
Hatina said the fund will use its resources for promotion campaigns and ruled out the possibility of using the fund to subsidise Slovak export prices to make its products more competitive abroad.
"I guarantee you that no project demanding subsidising export prices will pass the fund's board," he said.

The fund's nine-member board, which will evaluate projects and select those for support, consists of economics and finance ministry officials and representatives of large exporters, such as steel maker VSZ, tyre producer Matador Puchov or Slovnaft.
At least 70 percent of the funds should be used to help finance presentation of Slovak products on foreign markets, such as world trade fairs, Hatina said.
Slovakia posted a foreign trade deficit of 64.54 billion crowns in 1996, after a 5.69 billion crown shortfall in 1995

The country's foreign trade balance showed a deficit of 7.06 billion crowns in January 1997, compared with a 2.13 billion crown gap in January last year. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
